findings.evidence: features/007-prune-skill/007-prune-skill-prd.md:R3 + AC-3 — R3 names the non-negotiable rule staleness boundary as 'the rule's body's *Why* section cites a `decision-log.md` entry by title AND that decision-log entry has been superseded'. AC-3 elaborates: 'the skill scans every `decision-log.md` entry's `**Related:**` field for the literal substring `Supersedes: "{cited title}"`'. The detection of 'cites a decision-log entry by title' is left undefined — does the skill (a) parse the rule's *Why* section as free-text and look for any quoted string that exact-matches a decision-log entry's H2 title, (b) require a structured citation pattern (e.g. `(see decision-log entry 'X')` or a markdown link `[decision-log: X](../decision-log.md#x)`), or (c) require the rule's frontmatter to carry an explicit `decision_link: "X"` field? The three interpretations produce different candidate sets. Reading `examples/docs/specflow/admin/rules/guidelines.md`: the existing `PREFER_LOCAL_TESTS` rule cites 'See decision-log entry 2026-02-14' (date-based); `PREFER_COMPOSITION_OVER_INHERITANCE` cites 'See decision-log entry 2026-01-08' (date-based). Neither cites by title; both cite by date. The PRD's title-based citation detection would not match either existing rule.
findings.claim: Unstated assumption — R3 + AC-3 specify title-based citation detection but the existing rules in the worked example cite decision-log entries by date, not title. Think-Before-Coding line: 'state assumptions explicitly.' The PRD silently picked title-based detection without accounting for the existing convention OR documenting the migration path. A fresh agent implementing R3 would scan rule bodies for quoted titles, find zero matches against the existing rules, and conclude no rules are stale — false negative. Worse: the supersede-link prefix `Supersedes: "{cited title}"` is title-based by `specflow:decision`'s R6 + AC-5, which means the supersede signal IS title-based; the rule citation convention is date-based; the two don't connect. The implementation needs a bridge — either (a) require future rule citations to use titles, with a migration step for existing date-based citations, or (b) the staleness detection has to resolve both citation styles.
findings.proposed_change: Edit R3 and AC-3 to name the citation-resolution strategy explicitly. Two clean shapes: (a) **Tolerate both citation styles.** R3: 'A non-negotiable rule is a prune candidate iff its body's *Why* section cites a `decision-log.md` entry by title (quoted) OR by date (`YYYY-MM-DD` format), AND the cited entry has been superseded.' Add a citation-resolution helper that parses both shapes — extract quoted titles AND `YYYY-MM-DD` dates from the rule body; for each extracted reference, find the matching decision-log entry; check supersession against that entry's title. (b) **Require title-based citations going forward; flag date-based citations for migration.** R3 stays title-only; add a new requirement: 'Rules whose *Why* section cites only by date (no title quoted) emit a one-line migration warning during pre-flight: `Rule {id} cites decision-log by date only; supersession detection requires title citation. See migration guide.`' Option (a) is the smaller surgical change — accommodates the existing convention without forcing a corpus-wide migration. Option (b) is purer but requires a separate migration skill. Either closes the unstated-assumption gap; option (a) is recommended.
